It was also said that it is a resumption; the first is preferable. His saying ﴿recited to him﴾ is in the accusative place as a circumstantial clause. Then he persists in his disbelief and remains in what he was upon, while being arrogant, that is: he persists in his disbelief, magnifying himself in his soul against submitting to the truth. Al-Israr (persistence) is taken from the persistence of a donkey upon its female herd, which is that it bends over it with its ears laid back.

Muqatil said: When he hears something of the verses of the Qur'an, he takes them in mockery. The clause ﴿as if he had not heard it﴾ is in the accusative place as a circumstantial clause, or it is a new clause. ﴿An﴾ here is the lightened form of the heavy one, and its noun is an omitted pronoun of the matter. ﴿So give him tidings of a painful punishment﴾. This is of the category of sarcasm, that is: so give him tidings, in view of his persistence, his arrogance, his not listening to the signs, of a punishment severe in pain.

﴿And when he knows something of Our signs﴾. Al-Jumhur read ʿalima with a fatha on the ʿayn and a kasra on the lam, lightened, in the active voice. Qatada and Matar al-Warraq read it in the passive voice.

The meaning: when knowledge of something of the signs of Allah reaches him, he takes them (the signs) in mockery. It was said: the pronoun in ﴿took them﴾ refers to ﴿something﴾, because it is an expression for the signs. The first is preferable.

The indication by His saying ﴿those﴾ is to every sinful liar characterized by these attributes. ﴿For them is a humiliating punishment﴾ because of what they did of persistence and arrogance towards hearing the signs of Allah and taking them in mockery. The humiliating punishment is that which includes abasement and disgrace.

﴿Behind them is Hell﴾, that is: behind what they are in of exalting themselves by the world and being arrogant towards the truth is Hell. For it is before them, since they are heading toward it. He expressed "behind" for "before," as in His saying: ﴿Behind him is Hell﴾ [Ibrahim: 16], and the saying of the poet:

Is it not behind me, if my death is delayed?

It was said: He made it so in consideration of their turning away from it, as if it were behind them.

﴿Nor will there avail them what they earned, anything﴾, that is: there will not repel from them what they earned of their wealth and their children any of the punishment of Allah, nor will it benefit them in any way of the ways of benefit. ﴿Nor what they took besides Allah as protectors﴾ is conjoined to ﴿what they earned﴾, that is: nor will there avail them what they took besides Allah as protectors of the idols. The word ﴿ma﴾ in both places is either a verbal noun or a relative pronoun, and the addition of ﴿nor﴾ in the second clause is for emphasis. ﴿And for them is a great punishment﴾ in Hell, which is behind them.

﴿This is guidance﴾ is a new clause consisting of a subject and predicate, meaning: this Qur'an is guidance for those who are guided by it. ﴿And those who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord﴾, the Qur'anic signs, ﴿for them is a punishment of painful wrath﴾. Al-Rijz is the most severe punishment.

Al-Jumhur read ﴿painful﴾ in the genitive as an attribute of ﴿wrath﴾. Ibn Kathir, Hafs, and Ibn Muhaysin read it in the nominative as an attribute of ﴿punishment﴾.

﴿Allah is He who subjected the sea for you﴾, that is: He made it in a state by which you are enabled to ride upon it. ﴿That the ships may run upon it by His command﴾, that is: by His permission and His enabling you. ﴿And that you may seek of His bounty﴾ by trade at times, and by diving for pearls, and by fishing, and other than that. ﴿And perhaps you will be grateful﴾, that is: so that you may be grateful for the blessings which come to you through this subjection of the sea.

﴿And He subjected for you what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, all of it from Him﴾, that is: He subjected for His servants what He created in His heavens and His earth, (p-1357) of what their welfare depends upon and by which their livelihoods are sustained.

Of the creatures of the heavens that He subjected for them: the sun, the moon, the shining stars, the rain, the clouds, and the winds. The accusative of ﴿all﴾ is as a circumstantial clause from ﴿what is in the heavens and what is in the earth﴾, or it is an emphasis of it. His saying ﴿from Him﴾ may be connected to an omitted word which is an attribute of ﴿all﴾, meaning: existing from Him. It may be connected to ﴿subjected﴾. It may be a circumstantial clause from ﴿what is in the heavens﴾, or a predicate of an omitted subject.

The meaning: all of that is mercy from Him to His servants. ﴿Indeed in that which is mentioned of subjection are signs for a people who reflect.﴾ He specified those who reflect because no one benefits from them except one who reflects upon them, for he moves from reflection to inference from them toward monotheism.

﴿Say to those who believe: forgive those who do not hope for the Days of Allah﴾, that is: say to them, "Forgive, they will be forgiven." It was said: it is with the omission of the lam, and the estimate is: "Say to them, so that they may forgive."

The meaning: say to them, "Let them overlook those who do not hope for the events of Allah against His enemies," that is, they do not anticipate them. The meaning of "hope" here is fear. It was said: it is in its true meaning.

The meaning: they do not hope for His reward in the times which Allah appointed for the reward of the believers. The first is preferable.

The days are expressed to denote events, as has already been mentioned in the explanation of His saying: ﴿And remind them of the Days of Allah﴾ [Ibrahim: 5]. Muqatil said: they do not fear the like of the punishment of Allah upon the nations of the past, because they do not believe in it, and so they do not fear its punishment.

It was said: the meaning is: they do not hope for the help of Allah for His allies, and His striking down of His enemies. It was said: they do not fear the resurrection.

It was said: the verse is abrogated by the verse of the sword.

﴿That He may recompense a people for what they used to earn﴾. Ibn Amir, Hamzah, and al-Kisa'i read "li-najziya" with the nun, that is: "that We may recompense," meaning: We Ourselves.

The rest of the Seven read it with the yā' (third person), in the active voice, that is: "that Allah may recompense."

Abu Ja'far, Shayba, and Asim read it with the yā' in the passive voice, with the accusative of ﴿a people﴾. It was said: the substitute for the doer is the verbal noun of the verb, that is: "that recompense may be made to a people." It was said: the substitute is the prepositional phrase, as in the saying of the poet:

And if a poor woman bore a pup of a dog, the dogs would be cursed because of that pup.

Al-Akhfash and the Kufans permitted this, while the Basrans forbade it. The clause is a ground for the command to forgive. The people intended are the believers, who were commanded to forgive, so that Allah may recompense them on the Day of Resurrection for what they earned in the world of good deeds, among which is patience with the harm of the disbelievers, overlooking them, restraining anger, and enduring what is hateful.

It was said: the meaning is: that He may recompense the disbelievers for what they did of evil deeds, as if He said: "Do not repay them, so that We may repay them." The first is preferable.

Then He mentioned the believers and their deeds, and the polytheists and their deeds, saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for himself; and whoever does evil, it is against himself﴾. The meaning: the deed of each group, whether good or bad, does not go beyond its doer to another, and in this is encouragement and warning. ﴿Then to your Lord you will be returned﴾, so He will recompense each according to his deed: if it is good, then good, and if it is evil, then evil.

Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu al-Shaykh in "al-Azamah" reported through the route of Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿all of it from Him﴾, that he said: "From Him is the light, the sun, and the moon."

Ibn Jarir reported from him concerning the verse, that he said: "Everything is from Allah."

Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), and al-Bayhaqi in "al-Asma' wa al-Sifat" reported from Tawus, who said: A man came to Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As and asked him: "Of what was creation created?" He said: "Of water, light, darkness, air, and earth." He said: "Of what were these created?" He said: "I do not know."

Then the man came to ʿAbdullah ibn al-Zubayr and asked him, and he gave the same answer as ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr. Then he came to Ibn ʿAbbas and asked him, "From what were the creatures created?" He said, "From water, light, darkness, wind and earth." He said, "From what were these created?" Ibn ʿAbbas then recited: ﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, all of it from Him﴾. The man said, "None could have brought this except a man from the household of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Say to those who believe that they should forgive﴾ up to the end of the verse, that he said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to turn away from the polytheists when they harmed him, and they used to mock him and deny him. So Allah commanded him to fight the polytheists entirely, and this is among the abrogated (mansukh) rulings.

﴿And We certainly gave the Children of Israel the Book, the judgement (al-hukm) and prophethood, and We provided them with good things and preferred them over the worlds﴾. ﴿And We gave them clear proofs concerning the matter, and they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of rivalry among themselves. Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ﴾. ﴿Then We placed you on a path (shari'ah) of the matter, so follow it, and do not follow the desires of those who do not know﴾. ﴿Indeed they will not avail you anything against Allah. And indeed the wrongdoers are allies of one another, while Allah is the Ally of the God-fearing﴾. ﴿This is insight for mankind, and guidance and mercy for a people who have certainty﴾. ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will treat them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal in their living and their dying? Evil is their judgement﴾. ﴿And Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth, and so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged﴾. ﴿Have you seen him who takes his own desire as his god, and Allah has led him astray knowingly, and has sealed his hearing and his heart, and placed a covering over his sight? Who then will guide him after Allah? Will you not take heed?﴾ ﴿And they say: "There is nothing but our life of this world; we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time." And they have no knowledge of that; they only conjecture﴾. ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, their only argument is to say: "Bring our fathers, if you are truthful."﴾ ﴿Say: "Allah gives you life, then makes you die, then gathers you to the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt," but most people do not know﴾.

His saying: ﴿And We certainly gave the Children of Israel the Book, the judgement and prophethood﴾. The Book here is the Torah; the judgement (al-hukm) is the understanding and jurisprudence (fiqh) by which judgement is made among people and their disputes are settled; prophethood refers to those prophets whom Allah sent among them. ﴿And We provided them with good things﴾, i.e., the delightful things which Allah made lawful for them, among which were the manna and the quails. ﴿And preferred them over the worlds﴾, i.e., over the people of their time, since We gave them what We did not give to others besides them, such as the splitting of the sea and the like.

The explanation of this has already preceded in Surat al-Dukhan.

﴿And We gave them clear proofs concerning the matter﴾, i.e., clear laws concerning the lawful and the unlawful, or manifest miracles. It was also said: knowledge of the sending of the Prophet (ﷺ), the signs of his prophethood, and the specification of his place of migration. ﴿So they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them﴾, i.e., the disagreement among them about that matter occurred only after knowledge had come to them through its explanation and clarification of its meaning; thus they made what should have removed disagreement into the cause of its establishment. It was said: the "knowledge" here refers to Yusha ibn Nun, for some of them believed in him and some disbelieved. It was also said: it refers to the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), and they differed about it out of envy and rivalry. It was also said: rivalry among some of them against others, through seeking leadership. ﴿Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ﴾ regarding matters of religion, rewarding the doer of good for his good and the doer of evil for his evil.

﴿Then We placed you on a path (shari'ah) of the matter﴾. Shari'ah linguistically means a way (madhhab), a creed (millah) and a method (minhaj); it is said of the watering-place of water, which is the place where its drinkers come, a shari'ah; and from it comes "al-shari'" (the legislator), because it is a path to the goal. So the meaning of shari'ah here is what Allah prescribed for His servants of the religion, and its plural is shara'i'. That is: We placed you, O Muhammad, upon a clear method of the matter of religion that brings you to the truth, so follow it and act by its rulings with your community. ﴿And do not follow the desires of those who do not know﴾, i.e., the monotheism of Allah and His laws for His servants; they are the disbelievers of Quraysh and whoever agreed with them.

﴿Indeed they will not avail you anything against Allah﴾, i.e., they cannot repel from you anything of what Allah intends for you if you follow their desires. ﴿And indeed the wrongdoers are allies of one another﴾, i.e., helpers, each supporting the other. Ibn Zayd said: the hypocrites are allies of the Jews. ﴿While Allah is the Ally of the God-fearing﴾, i.e., their helper; and by "the God-fearing" are meant those who guarded against polytheism and sins.

The demonstrative in His saying "This" refers either to the Qur'an or to following the shari'ah. It is the subject, and its predicate is "is insight for mankind", i.e., proofs and indications for them concerning what they need of the rulings of religion; He made it as insight in the hearts. It is also read "these are insights", i.e., these verses, since the Qur'an has the same meaning as them, as the poet said:

"Ask the Banu Asad what this sound (al-sawt) is,"

since al-sawt means the cry. ﴿And guidance﴾, i.e., right direction and a path leading to Paradise for whoever acts by it. ﴿And mercy﴾ from Allah in the Hereafter, ﴿for a people who have certainty﴾, i.e., it is their nature to have certainty and to be free of doubt and wavering by doubts.

﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think﴾. "Am" here is the disjunctive one, presumed to be with "bal" and the hamzah; what is in it of the meaning of "bal" indicates the transition from the first statement to the second, and the hamzah is for denouncing the supposition. "Ijtirah" means acquiring, and from it comes "al-jawarih" (the limbs); it was mentioned in Surat al-Ma'idah. The sentence is resumed to explain the contrast between the two states of evildoers and doers of good, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿that We would treat them like those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, i.e., We would make them equal, despite their committing evil deeds, with the people of good deeds. ﴿Equal in their living and their dying﴾ in the abode of this world and in the Hereafter. "No, they are not equal, for the state of the people of felicity in both is other than the state of the people of wretchedness."

It was also said: the meaning is a denial that they would be equal in dying as they were equal in living.

The majority read "sawaʾun" with raising, as a predicate preceding its subject, the subject being "their living and their dying", and the meaning: a denial of their supposition that their living and their dying are equal. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read "sawaʾan" with the accusative, as a state of the pronoun hidden in the preposition-and-object in His saying "like those who believe", or as a second object of "hasiba". Abu ʿUbayd preferred the accusative reading and said its meaning is "We would make them equal." Al-Aʿmash and ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar read "mamatahum" with the accusative, meaning "equal in their living and their dying"; when the preposition was dropped, it took the accusative; or it is a substitute of the object of "najʿaluhum", a substitution of inclusion. ﴿Evil is their judgement﴾, i.e., evil is this judgement of theirs which they passed.

﴿And Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth﴾, i.e., with the truth that requires justice among the servants. The place of "bi-al-haqq" is accusative as a state of the agent or of the object, or the "ba'" is causal. His saying ﴿and so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned﴾ may be upon the truth, since each of them is a cause, so He joined a cause to a cause; it may also be conjoined to an omitted element, the estimate being: Allah created the heavens and the earth so that by them He might show His power, and so that they may be recompensed; and the lam may be of result. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾, i.e., the souls indicated by "every soul" will not be wronged by a reduction of reward or an increase of punishment.

Then He, glorified is He, marvelled at the state of the disbelievers, saying: ﴿Have you seen him who takes his desire as his god?﴾ Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: that disbeliever takes as his religion whatever he desires, so he does not desire anything without pursuing it. ʿIkrimah said: he worships what he desires or finds good; when he finds something good and it pleases him, he takes it as a god.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: one of them would worship a stone, and when he saw something better than it he would discard it and worship the other. ﴿And Allah has led him astray knowingly﴾, i.e., with a knowledge He had. It was said: the meaning is: He led him astray from reward with knowledge on His part that he does not deserve it. Muqatil said: with knowledge from Him that he is astray, because He knows that the idol neither benefits nor harms.

Al-Zajjaj said: "with ill in His knowledge," that he is astray before He created him. The place of "ʿalā ʿilmin" is accusative as a state of the agent or the object. ﴿And He has sealed his hearing and his heart﴾, i.e., He stamped upon his hearing so that he does not hear the admonition, and stamped upon his heart so that he does not comprehend guidance. ﴿And placed a covering over his sight﴾, i.e., a veil, so that he does not see right direction.

The majority read "ghishawatan" with an alif and a kasra on the ghayn. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "ghashwatan" without alif and with a fatha on the ghayn, and from it is the poet's saying:

"If you had clothed me in a covering (ghashwah), I had certainly, for a while, inclined to you in affection."

Ibn Mas'ud and al-A'mash read like the majority's reading with a fatha on the ghayn, and this is the dialect of Rabi'ah. Al-Hasan and ʿIkrimah read it with a damma, and this is the dialect of ʿUkl. ﴿Then who will guide him after Allah?﴾, i.e., after Allah's misguiding him. ﴿Will you not take heed?﴾, a heeding of consideration, so that you may know the reality of the situation.

Then He, glorified is He, explained some of their ignorance and their errors, saying: ﴿And they say: "There is nothing but our life of this world"﴾, i.e., life is nothing but this life in which we are. ﴿We die and we live﴾, i.e., death befalls us and life in it; there is no life beyond that. It was said: we die ourselves, and our children live after us. It was said: we are first non-living drops, then we become living.

It was also said: there is inversion and reversal in the verse, i.e., "we live and we die", and Ibn Mas'ud read it so. In any case, their purpose in this saying is the denial of resurrection and the denial of the Hereafter. ﴿And nothing destroys us except time (al-dahr)﴾, i.e., nothing but the passing of days and nights. Mujahid said: he means years and days. Qatadah said: nothing but lifespan (al-ʿumr); the meaning is the same. Qutrub said: the meaning is "nothing destroys us except death". ʿIkrimah said: "nothing destroys us except Allah."

﴿And they have no knowledge of that﴾, i.e., they did not utter this saying except as doubters, not knowing the reality.

Then He explained that this proceeded from them and not from knowledge, saying: ﴿They only conjecture﴾, i.e., they are a people whose utmost is conjecture, so they speak only by it and rely only upon it.

﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them﴾, i.e., when the verses of the Qur'an are recited to the polytheists, being clear, manifest in meaning and in indication regarding resurrection, ﴿their only argument is to say: "Bring our fathers, if you are truthful" that we will be raised after death﴾, i.e., they had no argument nor any clinging except this false saying, which is not an argument in anything; he called it an argument only mockingly toward them.

The majority read "ḥujjatahum" with the accusative as the predicate of "kāna", with its subject being "illā an qālū". Zayd ibn ʿAli, ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmar read "ḥujjatuhum" with the nominative, as the subject of "kāna".

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to respond to them, saying: ﴿Say: "Allah gives you life"﴾, i.e., in this world, ﴿then makes you die﴾ at the end of your terms, ﴿then gathers you to the Day of Resurrection﴾ by the raising and the rising, ﴿about which there is no doubt﴾, i.e., concerning your gathering; for whoever is able to originate creation is able to restore it. ﴿But most people do not know﴾ this, and therefore doubt about resurrection arose in them, and they came up in repelling it with what is weaker than the spider's web. Had they looked with proper looking, they would have attained certain knowledge, the doubt would have left them, and they would have relieved themselves from the entanglement of doubt and bewilderment.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Then We placed you on a path of the matter﴾, that he said: "upon guidance in the matter of his religion."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿equal in their living and their dying﴾, that he said: "The believer is a believer in this world and the Hereafter, and the disbeliever is a disbeliever in this world and the Hereafter."

Al-Shawkani, *Fath al-Qadir*, on surah 45, verses 16–27 (part 3 of 3):

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Asma' wa al-Sifat* narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Have you seen him who has taken his desire as his god?﴾ He said: "That is the disbeliever who took his religion without guidance from Allah or any proof." ﴿And Allah has misled him with knowledge﴾ means: He misled him in His prior knowledge.

Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, who declared it authentic (ṣaḥḥaḥahu), and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him that he said: "A man among the Arabs used to worship a stone. Whenever he found something better than it, he would take that and throw away the other. So Allah revealed: ﴿Have you seen him who has taken his desire as his god?﴾"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Hurayrah that he said: "The people of the Jahiliyyah used to say, 'Only the night and the day destroy us.' So Allah said in His Book: ﴿And they said, 'There is nothing but our life of this world: we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time.'﴾ Allah said: 'The son of Adam harms Me; he curses time, while I am time. In My hand is the affair; I turn the night and the day.'"

Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'The son of Adam harms Me; he curses time, while I am time. In My hand is the affair; I turn the night and the day.'"

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 45, verses 16–27 (part 1 of 3):

It is Makkan in its entirety according to al-Hasan, Jabir, and Ikrimah.

Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr that it was revealed in Makkah. It is also reported from Ibn Abbas and Qatada that they both said: "Except for one verse within it, which is His saying: ﴿for those who believe﴾ (up to) ﴿the Days of Allah﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 14]. That verse was revealed in Madinah concerning Umar ibn al-Khattab, as will come."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying: Ha Mim. The discussion of this opening (al-fatihah) and its i'rab (grammatical analysis) has already been made at the opening of surah Ghafir and what follows it. If it is taken as the name of the surah, then its place (in i'rab) is in the nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject or as a subject. If it is taken as separate letters listed in the manner of enumeration, then it has no place in i'rab.

His saying: ﴿The revelation of the Book﴾. On the first view it is a second predicate; on the second view it is the predicate of the subject; on the third view it is the predicate of an omitted subject, or a subject whose predicate is ﴿from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾.

Then He, glorified is He, informed of what indicates His overwhelming power, saying: ﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers﴾. That is: in them themselves, for they are among the varieties of signs, or in their creation.

Al-Zajjaj said: What indicates that the meaning is in the creation of the heavens and the earth is His saying: ﴿And in your creation﴾, that is, in the creation of yourselves through varied stages.

Muqatil said: from dust, then from a drop of semen, until one becomes a human being. ﴿And what He disperses of living creatures are signs﴾, that is: and in the creation of what He disperses of living creatures. The nominative of ﴿signs﴾ is because it is a postponed subject, and its predicate is the adverbial phrase before it. Al-Jumhur (the majority of readers) read it in the nominative, while Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ﴿ayat﴾ in the accusative, as a conjunction with the noun of inna (indeed), and the predicate is his saying ﴿and in your creation﴾, as if it were said: "Indeed, in your creation and in what He disperses of living creatures are signs." Or it is an emphasis of the first ﴿signs﴾.

Al-Jumhur also read ﴿signs for a people who have certainty﴾ in the nominative, while Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it in the accusative, with their agreement on the genitive in ﴿the alternation﴾. As for the genitive in ﴿the alternation﴾, it is by the assumption of a particle of the genitive, that is: "and in the alternation of night and day are signs." Whoever reads ﴿signs﴾ in the nominative, it is as a subject, and its predicate is ﴿in the alternation﴾. As for the accusative, it is from the category of conjunction to two operands of two different governing words.

Al-Farra' said: The nominative is by resumption after inna, as the Arabs say: "Indeed for me upon you is wealth, and upon your brother is wealth," they put the second in the accusative and in the nominative. The grammarians have lengthy discussion on this point.

The investigation of the issue of conjunction to two operands of two different governing words, and the arguments of those who permit it and the rebuttals of those who forbid it, is established in the science of grammar and expounded in its extended works.

The meaning of ﴿what He disperses of living creatures﴾ is what He spreads out and scatters.

﴿And the alternation of night and day﴾ is their succession or their difference in length and shortness. His saying ﴿and what Allah sends down from the sky of provision﴾ is conjoined to ﴿alternation﴾. The provision is the rain, because it is the cause of everything by which Allah provides for His servants. The reviving of the earth is the bringing forth of its vegetation, and its dying is its being barren of vegetation. The meaning of ﴿the turning of the winds﴾ is that they blow at times from one direction and at other times from another, and at times they are hot and at other times cold, and at times beneficial and at other times harmful.

﴿These are the signs of Allah which We recite to you﴾, that is: these mentioned signs are the proofs and evidences of Allah. The place of ﴿which We recite to you﴾ is the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal), and it is permissible that it be in the nominative place as the predicate of the demonstrative noun. ﴿The signs of Allah﴾ is an explanation of it or an appositive to it. His saying ﴿in truth﴾ is a circumstantial clause from the doer of ﴿We recite﴾ or from its object, that is: "those who are truthful," or "those connected with truth." It is also permissible that the bā' (in) be causal, so that it is connected to the verb itself.

﴿Then in what statement after Allah and His signs will they believe?﴾ That is: after the statement of Allah and after His signs. It was said: the intended meaning is "after the signs of Allah." The mention of the noble Name is only for the purpose of magnifying the signs, and so it is of the type of: "Zayd impressed me, and his generosity."

It was said: the intended meaning is "after the statement of Allah," which is the Qur'an, as in His saying: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement﴾ [al-Zumar: 23], and this is what is meant by the signs. The conjunction is merely for the mere difference of designation.

Al-Jumhur read ﴿will they believe﴾ with the second person (tu'minun), while Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with the third person (yu'minun).

The meaning is: "they believe in what statement?" It is placed before it only because interrogation has the front position in speech.

﴿Woe to every sinful liar﴾, that is: to every liar who commits much sin and commits what necessitates it. Al-Wayl is a valley in Hell.

Then He described this liar with another attribute, saying: ﴿He hears the signs of Allah recited to him﴾. It was said: ﴿hears﴾ is in the accusative place as a circumstantial clause. It was also said that it is a resumption; the first is preferable. His saying ﴿recited to him﴾ is in the accusative place as a circumstantial clause. Then he persists in his disbelief and remains in what he was upon, while being arrogant, that is: he persists in his disbelief, magnifying himself in his soul against submitting to the truth. Al-Israr (persistence) is taken from the persistence of a donkey upon its female herd, which is that it bends over it with its ears laid back.

Muqatil said: When he hears something of the verses of the Qur'an, he takes them in mockery. The clause ﴿as if he had not heard it﴾ is in the accusative place as a circumstantial clause, or it is a new clause. ﴿An﴾ here is the lightened form of the heavy one, and its noun is an omitted pronoun of the matter. ﴿So give him tidings of a painful punishment﴾. This is of the category of sarcasm, that is: so give him tidings, in view of his persistence, his arrogance, his not listening to the signs, of a punishment severe in pain.

﴿And when he knows something of Our signs﴾. Al-Jumhur read ʿalima with a fatha on the ʿayn and a kasra on the lam, lightened, in the active voice. Qatada and Matar al-Warraq read it in the passive voice.

The meaning: when knowledge of something of the signs of Allah reaches him, he takes them (the signs) in mockery. It was said: the pronoun in ﴿took them﴾ refers to ﴿something﴾, because it is an expression for the signs. The first is preferable.

The indication by His saying ﴿those﴾ is to every sinful liar characterized by these attributes. ﴿For them is a humiliating punishment﴾ because of what they did of persistence and arrogance towards hearing the signs of Allah and taking them in mockery. The humiliating punishment is that which includes abasement and disgrace.

﴿Behind them is Hell﴾, that is: behind what they are in of exalting themselves by the world and being arrogant towards the truth is Hell. For it is before them, since they are heading toward it. He expressed "behind" for "before," as in His saying: ﴿Behind him is Hell﴾ [Ibrahim: 16], and the saying of the poet:

Is it not behind me, if my death is delayed?

It was said: He made it so in consideration of their turning away from it, as if it were behind them.

﴿Nor will there avail them what they earned, anything﴾, that is: there will not repel from them what they earned of their wealth and their children any of the punishment of Allah, nor will it benefit them in any way of the ways of benefit. ﴿Nor what they took besides Allah as protectors﴾ is conjoined to ﴿what they earned﴾, that is: nor will there avail them what they took besides Allah as protectors of the idols. The word ﴿ma﴾ in both places is either a verbal noun or a relative pronoun, and the addition of ﴿nor﴾ in the second clause is for emphasis. ﴿And for them is a great punishment﴾ in Hell, which is behind them.

﴿This is guidance﴾ is a new clause consisting of a subject and predicate, meaning: this Qur'an is guidance for those who are guided by it. ﴿And those who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord﴾, the Qur'anic signs, ﴿for them is a punishment of painful wrath﴾. Al-Rijz is the most severe punishment.

Al-Jumhur read ﴿painful﴾ in the genitive as an attribute of ﴿wrath﴾. Ibn Kathir, Hafs, and Ibn Muhaysin read it in the nominative as an attribute of ﴿punishment﴾.

﴿Allah is He who subjected the sea for you﴾, that is: He made it in a state by which you are enabled to ride upon it. ﴿That the ships may run upon it by His command﴾, that is: by His permission and His enabling you. ﴿And that you may seek of His bounty﴾ by trade at times, and by diving for pearls, and by fishing, and other than that. ﴿And perhaps you will be grateful﴾, that is: so that you may be grateful for the blessings which come to you through this subjection of the sea.

﴿And He subjected for you what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, all of it from Him﴾, that is: He subjected for His servants what He created in His heavens and His earth, (p-1357) of what their welfare depends upon and by which their livelihoods are sustained.

Of the creatures of the heavens that He subjected for them: the sun, the moon, the shining stars, the rain, the clouds, and the winds. The accusative of ﴿all﴾ is as a circumstantial clause from ﴿what is in the heavens and what is in the earth﴾, or it is an emphasis of it. His saying ﴿from Him﴾ may be connected to an omitted word which is an attribute of ﴿all﴾, meaning: existing from Him. It may be connected to ﴿subjected﴾. It may be a circumstantial clause from ﴿what is in the heavens﴾, or a predicate of an omitted subject.

The meaning: all of that is mercy from Him to His servants. ﴿Indeed in that which is mentioned of subjection are signs for a people who reflect.﴾ He specified those who reflect because no one benefits from them except one who reflects upon them, for he moves from reflection to inference from them toward monotheism.

﴿Say to those who believe: forgive those who do not hope for the Days of Allah﴾, that is: say to them, "Forgive, they will be forgiven." It was said: it is with the omission of the lam, and the estimate is: "Say to them, so that they may forgive."

The meaning: say to them, "Let them overlook those who do not hope for the events of Allah against His enemies," that is, they do not anticipate them. The meaning of "hope" here is fear. It was said: it is in its true meaning.

The meaning: they do not hope for His reward in the times which Allah appointed for the reward of the believers. The first is preferable.

The days are expressed to denote events, as has already been mentioned in the explanation of His saying: ﴿And remind them of the Days of Allah﴾ [Ibrahim: 5]. Muqatil said: they do not fear the like of the punishment of Allah upon the nations of the past, because they do not believe in it, and so they do not fear its punishment.

It was said: the meaning is: they do not hope for the help of Allah for His allies, and His striking down of His enemies. It was said: they do not fear the resurrection.

It was said: the verse is abrogated by the verse of the sword.

﴿That He may recompense a people for what they used to earn﴾. Ibn Amir, Hamzah, and al-Kisa'i read "li-najziya" with the nun, that is: "that We may recompense," meaning: We Ourselves.

The rest of the Seven read it with the yā' (third person), in the active voice, that is: "that Allah may recompense."

Abu Ja'far, Shayba, and Asim read it with the yā' in the passive voice, with the accusative of ﴿a people﴾. It was said: the substitute for the doer is the verbal noun of the verb, that is: "that recompense may be made to a people." It was said: the substitute is the prepositional phrase, as in the saying of the poet:

And if a poor woman bore a pup of a dog, the dogs would be cursed because of that pup.

Al-Akhfash and the Kufans permitted this, while the Basrans forbade it. The clause is a ground for the command to forgive. The people intended are the believers, who were commanded to forgive, so that Allah may recompense them on the Day of Resurrection for what they earned in the world of good deeds, among which is patience with the harm of the disbelievers, overlooking them, restraining anger, and enduring what is hateful.

It was said: the meaning is: that He may recompense the disbelievers for what they did of evil deeds, as if He said: "Do not repay them, so that We may repay them." The first is preferable.

Then He mentioned the believers and their deeds, and the polytheists and their deeds, saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for himself; and whoever does evil, it is against himself﴾. The meaning: the deed of each group, whether good or bad, does not go beyond its doer to another, and in this is encouragement and warning. ﴿Then to your Lord you will be returned﴾, so He will recompense each according to his deed: if it is good, then good, and if it is evil, then evil.

Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu al-Shaykh in "al-Azamah" reported through the route of Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿all of it from Him﴾, that he said: "From Him is the light, the sun, and the moon."

Ibn Jarir reported from him concerning the verse, that he said: "Everything is from Allah."

Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), and al-Bayhaqi in "al-Asma' wa al-Sifat" reported from Tawus, who said: A man came to Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As and asked him: "Of what was creation created?" He said: "Of water, light, darkness, air, and earth." He said: "Of what were these created?" He said: "I do not know."

Then the man came to ʿAbdullah ibn al-Zubayr and asked him, and he gave the same answer as ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr. Then he came to Ibn ʿAbbas and asked him, "From what were the creatures created?" He said, "From water, light, darkness, wind and earth." He said, "From what were these created?" Ibn ʿAbbas then recited: ﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, all of it from Him﴾. The man said, "None could have brought this except a man from the household of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Say to those who believe that they should forgive﴾ up to the end of the verse, that he said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to turn away from the polytheists when they harmed him, and they used to mock him and deny him. So Allah commanded him to fight the polytheists entirely, and this is among the abrogated (mansukh) rulings.

﴿And We certainly gave the Children of Israel the Book, the judgement (al-hukm) and prophethood, and We provided them with good things and preferred them over the worlds﴾. ﴿And We gave them clear proofs concerning the matter, and they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of rivalry among themselves. Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ﴾. ﴿Then We placed you on a path (shari'ah) of the matter, so follow it, and do not follow the desires of those who do not know﴾. ﴿Indeed they will not avail you anything against Allah. And indeed the wrongdoers are allies of one another, while Allah is the Ally of the God-fearing﴾. ﴿This is insight for mankind, and guidance and mercy for a people who have certainty﴾. ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will treat them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal in their living and their dying? Evil is their judgement﴾. ﴿And Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth, and so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged﴾. ﴿Have you seen him who takes his own desire as his god, and Allah has led him astray knowingly, and has sealed his hearing and his heart, and placed a covering over his sight? Who then will guide him after Allah? Will you not take heed?﴾ ﴿And they say: "There is nothing but our life of this world; we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time." And they have no knowledge of that; they only conjecture﴾. ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, their only argument is to say: "Bring our fathers, if you are truthful."﴾ ﴿Say: "Allah gives you life, then makes you die, then gathers you to the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt," but most people do not know﴾.

His saying: ﴿And We certainly gave the Children of Israel the Book, the judgement and prophethood﴾. The Book here is the Torah; the judgement (al-hukm) is the understanding and jurisprudence (fiqh) by which judgement is made among people and their disputes are settled; prophethood refers to those prophets whom Allah sent among them. ﴿And We provided them with good things﴾, i.e., the delightful things which Allah made lawful for them, among which were the manna and the quails. ﴿And preferred them over the worlds﴾, i.e., over the people of their time, since We gave them what We did not give to others besides them, such as the splitting of the sea and the like.

The explanation of this has already preceded in Surat al-Dukhan.

﴿And We gave them clear proofs concerning the matter﴾, i.e., clear laws concerning the lawful and the unlawful, or manifest miracles. It was also said: knowledge of the sending of the Prophet (ﷺ), the signs of his prophethood, and the specification of his place of migration. ﴿So they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them﴾, i.e., the disagreement among them about that matter occurred only after knowledge had come to them through its explanation and clarification of its meaning; thus they made what should have removed disagreement into the cause of its establishment. It was said: the "knowledge" here refers to Yusha ibn Nun, for some of them believed in him and some disbelieved. It was also said: it refers to the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), and they differed about it out of envy and rivalry. It was also said: rivalry among some of them against others, through seeking leadership. ﴿Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ﴾ regarding matters of religion, rewarding the doer of good for his good and the doer of evil for his evil.

﴿Then We placed you on a path (shari'ah) of the matter﴾. Shari'ah linguistically means a way (madhhab), a creed (millah) and a method (minhaj); it is said of the watering-place of water, which is the place where its drinkers come, a shari'ah; and from it comes "al-shari'" (the legislator), because it is a path to the goal. So the meaning of shari'ah here is what Allah prescribed for His servants of the religion, and its plural is shara'i'. That is: We placed you, O Muhammad, upon a clear method of the matter of religion that brings you to the truth, so follow it and act by its rulings with your community. ﴿And do not follow the desires of those who do not know﴾, i.e., the monotheism of Allah and His laws for His servants; they are the disbelievers of Quraysh and whoever agreed with them.

﴿Indeed they will not avail you anything against Allah﴾, i.e., they cannot repel from you anything of what Allah intends for you if you follow their desires. ﴿And indeed the wrongdoers are allies of one another﴾, i.e., helpers, each supporting the other. Ibn Zayd said: the hypocrites are allies of the Jews. ﴿While Allah is the Ally of the God-fearing﴾, i.e., their helper; and by "the God-fearing" are meant those who guarded against polytheism and sins.

The demonstrative in His saying "This" refers either to the Qur'an or to following the shari'ah. It is the subject, and its predicate is "is insight for mankind", i.e., proofs and indications for them concerning what they need of the rulings of religion; He made it as insight in the hearts. It is also read "these are insights", i.e., these verses, since the Qur'an has the same meaning as them, as the poet said:

"Ask the Banu Asad what this sound (al-sawt) is,"

since al-sawt means the cry. ﴿And guidance﴾, i.e., right direction and a path leading to Paradise for whoever acts by it. ﴿And mercy﴾ from Allah in the Hereafter, ﴿for a people who have certainty﴾, i.e., it is their nature to have certainty and to be free of doubt and wavering by doubts.

﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think﴾. "Am" here is the disjunctive one, presumed to be with "bal" and the hamzah; what is in it of the meaning of "bal" indicates the transition from the first statement to the second, and the hamzah is for denouncing the supposition. "Ijtirah" means acquiring, and from it comes "al-jawarih" (the limbs); it was mentioned in Surat al-Ma'idah. The sentence is resumed to explain the contrast between the two states of evildoers and doers of good, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿that We would treat them like those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, i.e., We would make them equal, despite their committing evil deeds, with the people of good deeds. ﴿Equal in their living and their dying﴾ in the abode of this world and in the Hereafter. "No, they are not equal, for the state of the people of felicity in both is other than the state of the people of wretchedness."

It was also said: the meaning is a denial that they would be equal in dying as they were equal in living.

The majority read "sawaʾun" with raising, as a predicate preceding its subject, the subject being "their living and their dying", and the meaning: a denial of their supposition that their living and their dying are equal. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read "sawaʾan" with the accusative, as a state of the pronoun hidden in the preposition-and-object in His saying "like those who believe", or as a second object of "hasiba". Abu ʿUbayd preferred the accusative reading and said its meaning is "We would make them equal." Al-Aʿmash and ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar read "mamatahum" with the accusative, meaning "equal in their living and their dying"; when the preposition was dropped, it took the accusative; or it is a substitute of the object of "najʿaluhum", a substitution of inclusion. ﴿Evil is their judgement﴾, i.e., evil is this judgement of theirs which they passed.

﴿And Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth﴾, i.e., with the truth that requires justice among the servants. The place of "bi-al-haqq" is accusative as a state of the agent or of the object, or the "ba'" is causal. His saying ﴿and so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned﴾ may be upon the truth, since each of them is a cause, so He joined a cause to a cause; it may also be conjoined to an omitted element, the estimate being: Allah created the heavens and the earth so that by them He might show His power, and so that they may be recompensed; and the lam may be of result. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾, i.e., the souls indicated by "every soul" will not be wronged by a reduction of reward or an increase of punishment.

Then He, glorified is He, marvelled at the state of the disbelievers, saying: ﴿Have you seen him who takes his desire as his god?﴾ Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: that disbeliever takes as his religion whatever he desires, so he does not desire anything without pursuing it. ʿIkrimah said: he worships what he desires or finds good; when he finds something good and it pleases him, he takes it as a god.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: one of them would worship a stone, and when he saw something better than it he would discard it and worship the other. ﴿And Allah has led him astray knowingly﴾, i.e., with a knowledge He had. It was said: the meaning is: He led him astray from reward with knowledge on His part that he does not deserve it. Muqatil said: with knowledge from Him that he is astray, because He knows that the idol neither benefits nor harms.

Al-Zajjaj said: "with ill in His knowledge," that he is astray before He created him. The place of "ʿalā ʿilmin" is accusative as a state of the agent or the object. ﴿And He has sealed his hearing and his heart﴾, i.e., He stamped upon his hearing so that he does not hear the admonition, and stamped upon his heart so that he does not comprehend guidance. ﴿And placed a covering over his sight﴾, i.e., a veil, so that he does not see right direction.

The majority read "ghishawatan" with an alif and a kasra on the ghayn. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "ghashwatan" without alif and with a fatha on the ghayn, and from it is the poet's saying:

"If you had clothed me in a covering (ghashwah), I had certainly, for a while, inclined to you in affection."

Ibn Mas'ud and al-A'mash read like the majority's reading with a fatha on the ghayn, and this is the dialect of Rabi'ah. Al-Hasan and ʿIkrimah read it with a damma, and this is the dialect of ʿUkl. ﴿Then who will guide him after Allah?﴾, i.e., after Allah's misguiding him. ﴿Will you not take heed?﴾, a heeding of consideration, so that you may know the reality of the situation.

Then He, glorified is He, explained some of their ignorance and their errors, saying: ﴿And they say: "There is nothing but our life of this world"﴾, i.e., life is nothing but this life in which we are. ﴿We die and we live﴾, i.e., death befalls us and life in it; there is no life beyond that. It was said: we die ourselves, and our children live after us. It was said: we are first non-living drops, then we become living.

It was also said: there is inversion and reversal in the verse, i.e., "we live and we die", and Ibn Mas'ud read it so. In any case, their purpose in this saying is the denial of resurrection and the denial of the Hereafter. ﴿And nothing destroys us except time (al-dahr)﴾, i.e., nothing but the passing of days and nights. Mujahid said: he means years and days. Qatadah said: nothing but lifespan (al-ʿumr); the meaning is the same. Qutrub said: the meaning is "nothing destroys us except death". ʿIkrimah said: "nothing destroys us except Allah."

﴿And they have no knowledge of that﴾, i.e., they did not utter this saying except as doubters, not knowing the reality.

Then He explained that this proceeded from them and not from knowledge, saying: ﴿They only conjecture﴾, i.e., they are a people whose utmost is conjecture, so they speak only by it and rely only upon it.

﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them﴾, i.e., when the verses of the Qur'an are recited to the polytheists, being clear, manifest in meaning and in indication regarding resurrection, ﴿their only argument is to say: "Bring our fathers, if you are truthful" that we will be raised after death﴾, i.e., they had no argument nor any clinging except this false saying, which is not an argument in anything; he called it an argument only mockingly toward them.

The majority read "ḥujjatahum" with the accusative as the predicate of "kāna", with its subject being "illā an qālū". Zayd ibn ʿAli, ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmar read "ḥujjatuhum" with the nominative, as the subject of "kāna".

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to respond to them, saying: ﴿Say: "Allah gives you life"﴾, i.e., in this world, ﴿then makes you die﴾ at the end of your terms, ﴿then gathers you to the Day of Resurrection﴾ by the raising and the rising, ﴿about which there is no doubt﴾, i.e., concerning your gathering; for whoever is able to originate creation is able to restore it. ﴿But most people do not know﴾ this, and therefore doubt about resurrection arose in them, and they came up in repelling it with what is weaker than the spider's web. Had they looked with proper looking, they would have attained certain knowledge, the doubt would have left them, and they would have relieved themselves from the entanglement of doubt and bewilderment.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Then We placed you on a path of the matter﴾, that he said: "upon guidance in the matter of his religion."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿equal in their living and their dying﴾, that he said: "The believer is a believer in this world and the Hereafter, and the disbeliever is a disbeliever in this world and the Hereafter."

Al-Shawkani, *Fath al-Qadir*, on surah 45, verses 16–27 (part 3 of 3):

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Asma' wa al-Sifat* narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Have you seen him who has taken his desire as his god?﴾ He said: "That is the disbeliever who took his religion without guidance from Allah or any proof." ﴿And Allah has misled him with knowledge﴾ means: He misled him in His prior knowledge.

Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, who declared it authentic (ṣaḥḥaḥahu), and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him that he said: "A man among the Arabs used to worship a stone. Whenever he found something better than it, he would take that and throw away the other. So Allah revealed: ﴿Have you seen him who has taken his desire as his god?﴾"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Hurayrah that he said: "The people of the Jahiliyyah used to say, 'Only the night and the day destroy us.' So Allah said in His Book: ﴿And they said, 'There is nothing but our life of this world: we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time.'﴾ Allah said: 'The son of Adam harms Me; he curses time, while I am time. In My hand is the affair; I turn the night and the day.'"

Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'The son of Adam harms Me; he curses time, while I am time. In My hand is the affair; I turn the night and the day.'"

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 45, verses 16–27 (part 1 of 3):

It is Makkan in its entirety according to al-Hasan, Jabir, and Ikrimah.

Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr that it was revealed in Makkah. It is also reported from Ibn Abbas and Qatada that they both said: "Except for one verse within it, which is His saying: ﴿for those who believe﴾ (up to) ﴿the Days of Allah﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 14]. That verse was revealed in Madinah concerning Umar ibn al-Khattab, as will come."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying: Ha Mim. The discussion of this opening (al-fatihah) and its i'rab (grammatical analysis) has already been made at the opening of surah Ghafir and what follows it. If it is taken as the name of the surah, then its place (in i'rab) is in the nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject or as a subject. If it is taken as separate letters listed in the manner of enumeration, then it has no place in i'rab.

His saying: ﴿The revelation of the Book﴾. On the first view it is a second predicate; on the second view it is the predicate of the subject; on the third view it is the predicate of an omitted subject, or a subject whose predicate is ﴿from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾.

Then He, glorified is He, informed of what indicates His overwhelming power, saying: ﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers﴾. That is: in them themselves, for they are among the varieties of signs, or in their creation.

Al-Zajjaj said: What indicates that the meaning is in the creation of the heavens and the earth is His saying: ﴿And in your creation﴾, that is, in the creation of yourselves through varied stages.

Muqatil said: from dust, then from a drop of semen, until one becomes a human being. ﴿And what He disperses of living creatures are signs﴾, that is: and in the creation of what He disperses of living creatures. The nominative of ﴿signs﴾ is because it is a postponed subject, and its predicate is the adverbial phrase before it. Al-Jumhur (the majority of readers) read it in the nominative, while Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ﴿ayat﴾ in the accusative, as a conjunction with the noun of inna (indeed), and the predicate is his saying ﴿and in your creation﴾, as if it were said: "Indeed, in your creation and in what He disperses of living creatures are signs." Or it is an emphasis of the first ﴿signs﴾.

Al-Jumhur also read ﴿signs for a people who have certainty﴾ in the nominative, while Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it in the accusative, with their agreement on the genitive in ﴿the alternation﴾. As for the genitive in ﴿the alternation﴾, it is by the assumption of a particle of the genitive, that is: "and in the alternation of night and day are signs." Whoever reads ﴿signs﴾ in the nominative, it is as a subject, and its predicate is ﴿in the alternation﴾. As for the accusative, it is from the category of conjunction to two operands of two different governing words.

Al-Farra' said: The nominative is by resumption after inna, as the Arabs say: "Indeed for me upon you is wealth, and upon your brother is wealth," they put the second in the accusative and in the nominative. The grammarians have lengthy discussion on this point.

The investigation of the issue of conjunction to two operands of two different governing words, and the arguments of those who permit it and the rebuttals of those who forbid it, is established in the science of grammar and expounded in its extended works.

The meaning of ﴿what He disperses of living creatures﴾ is what He spreads out and scatters.

﴿And the alternation of night and day﴾ is their succession or their difference in length and shortness. His saying ﴿and what Allah sends down from the sky of provision﴾ is conjoined to ﴿alternation﴾. The provision is the rain, because it is the cause of everything by which Allah provides for His servants. The reviving of the earth is the bringing forth of its vegetation, and its dying is its being barren of vegetation. The meaning of ﴿the turning of the winds﴾ is that they blow at times from one direction and at other times from another, and at times they are hot and at other times cold, and at times beneficial and at other times harmful.

﴿These are the signs of Allah which We recite to you﴾, that is: these mentioned signs are the proofs and evidences of Allah. The place of ﴿which We recite to you﴾ is the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal), and it is permissible that it be in the nominative place as the predicate of the demonstrative noun. ﴿The signs of Allah﴾ is an explanation of it or an appositive to it. His saying ﴿in truth﴾ is a circumstantial clause from the doer of ﴿We recite﴾ or from its object, that is: "those who are truthful," or "those connected with truth." It is also permissible that the bā' (in) be causal, so that it is connected to the verb itself.

﴿Then in what statement after Allah and His signs will they believe?﴾ That is: after the statement of Allah and after His signs. It was said: the intended meaning is "after the signs of Allah." The mention of the noble Name is only for the purpose of magnifying the signs, and so it is of the type of: "Zayd impressed me, and his generosity."

It was said: the intended meaning is "after the statement of Allah," which is the Qur'an, as in His saying: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement﴾ [al-Zumar: 23], and this is what is meant by the signs. The conjunction is merely for the mere difference of designation.

Al-Jumhur read ﴿will they believe﴾ with the second person (tu'minun), while Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with the third person (yu'minun).

The meaning is: "they believe in what statement?" It is placed before it only because interrogation has the front position in speech.

﴿Woe to every sinful liar﴾, that is: to every liar who commits much sin and commits what necessitates it. Al-Wayl is a valley in Hell.

Then He described this liar with another attribute, saying: ﴿He hears the signs of Allah recited to him﴾. It was said: ﴿hears﴾ is in the accusative place as a circumstantial clause. It was also said that it is a resumption; the first is preferable. His saying ﴿recited to him﴾ is in the accusative place as a circumstantial clause. Then he persists in his disbelief and remains in what he was upon, while being arrogant, that is: he persists in his disbelief, magnifying himself in his soul against submitting to the truth. Al-Israr (persistence) is taken from the persistence of a donkey upon its female herd, which is that it bends over it with its ears laid back.

Muqatil said: When he hears something of the verses of the Qur'an, he takes them in mockery. The clause ﴿as if he had not heard it﴾ is in the accusative place as a circumstantial clause, or it is a new clause. ﴿An﴾ here is the lightened form of the heavy one, and its noun is an omitted pronoun of the matter. ﴿So give him tidings of a painful punishment﴾. This is of the category of sarcasm, that is: so give him tidings, in view of his persistence, his arrogance, his not listening to the signs, of a punishment severe in pain.

﴿And when he knows something of Our signs﴾. Al-Jumhur read ʿalima with a fatha on the ʿayn and a kasra on the lam, lightened, in the active voice. Qatada and Matar al-Warraq read it in the passive voice.

The meaning: when knowledge of something of the signs of Allah reaches him, he takes them (the signs) in mockery. It was said: the pronoun in ﴿took them﴾ refers to ﴿something﴾, because it is an expression for the signs. The first is preferable.

The indication by His saying ﴿those﴾ is to every sinful liar characterized by these attributes. ﴿For them is a humiliating punishment﴾ because of what they did of persistence and arrogance towards hearing the signs of Allah and taking them in mockery. The humiliating punishment is that which includes abasement and disgrace.

﴿Behind them is Hell﴾, that is: behind what they are in of exalting themselves by the world and being arrogant towards the truth is Hell. For it is before them, since they are heading toward it. He expressed "behind" for "before," as in His saying: ﴿Behind him is Hell﴾ [Ibrahim: 16], and the saying of the poet:

Is it not behind me, if my death is delayed?

It was said: He made it so in consideration of their turning away from it, as if it were behind them.

﴿Nor will there avail them what they earned, anything﴾, that is: there will not repel from them what they earned of their wealth and their children any of the punishment of Allah, nor will it benefit them in any way of the ways of benefit. ﴿Nor what they took besides Allah as protectors﴾ is conjoined to ﴿what they earned﴾, that is: nor will there avail them what they took besides Allah as protectors of the idols. The word ﴿ma﴾ in both places is either a verbal noun or a relative pronoun, and the addition of ﴿nor﴾ in the second clause is for emphasis. ﴿And for them is a great punishment﴾ in Hell, which is behind them.

﴿This is guidance﴾ is a new clause consisting of a subject and predicate, meaning: this Qur'an is guidance for those who are guided by it. ﴿And those who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord﴾, the Qur'anic signs, ﴿for them is a punishment of painful wrath﴾. Al-Rijz is the most severe punishment.

Al-Jumhur read ﴿painful﴾ in the genitive as an attribute of ﴿wrath﴾. Ibn Kathir, Hafs, and Ibn Muhaysin read it in the nominative as an attribute of ﴿punishment﴾.

﴿Allah is He who subjected the sea for you﴾, that is: He made it in a state by which you are enabled to ride upon it. ﴿That the ships may run upon it by His command﴾, that is: by His permission and His enabling you. ﴿And that you may seek of His bounty﴾ by trade at times, and by diving for pearls, and by fishing, and other than that. ﴿And perhaps you will be grateful﴾, that is: so that you may be grateful for the blessings which come to you through this subjection of the sea.

﴿And He subjected for you what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, all of it from Him﴾, that is: He subjected for His servants what He created in His heavens and His earth, (p-1357) of what their welfare depends upon and by which their livelihoods are sustained.

Of the creatures of the heavens that He subjected for them: the sun, the moon, the shining stars, the rain, the clouds, and the winds. The accusative of ﴿all﴾ is as a circumstantial clause from ﴿what is in the heavens and what is in the earth﴾, or it is an emphasis of it. His saying ﴿from Him﴾ may be connected to an omitted word which is an attribute of ﴿all﴾, meaning: existing from Him. It may be connected to ﴿subjected﴾. It may be a circumstantial clause from ﴿what is in the heavens﴾, or a predicate of an omitted subject.

The meaning: all of that is mercy from Him to His servants. ﴿Indeed in that which is mentioned of subjection are signs for a people who reflect.﴾ He specified those who reflect because no one benefits from them except one who reflects upon them, for he moves from reflection to inference from them toward monotheism.

﴿Say to those who believe: forgive those who do not hope for the Days of Allah﴾, that is: say to them, "Forgive, they will be forgiven." It was said: it is with the omission of the lam, and the estimate is: "Say to them, so that they may forgive."

The meaning: say to them, "Let them overlook those who do not hope for the events of Allah against His enemies," that is, they do not anticipate them. The meaning of "hope" here is fear. It was said: it is in its true meaning.

The meaning: they do not hope for His reward in the times which Allah appointed for the reward of the believers. The first is preferable.

The days are expressed to denote events, as has already been mentioned in the explanation of His saying: ﴿And remind them of the Days of Allah﴾ [Ibrahim: 5]. Muqatil said: they do not fear the like of the punishment of Allah upon the nations of the past, because they do not believe in it, and so they do not fear its punishment.

It was said: the meaning is: they do not hope for the help of Allah for His allies, and His striking down of His enemies. It was said: they do not fear the resurrection.

It was said: the verse is abrogated by the verse of the sword.

﴿That He may recompense a people for what they used to earn﴾. Ibn Amir, Hamzah, and al-Kisa'i read "li-najziya" with the nun, that is: "that We may recompense," meaning: We Ourselves.

The rest of the Seven read it with the yā' (third person), in the active voice, that is: "that Allah may recompense."

Abu Ja'far, Shayba, and Asim read it with the yā' in the passive voice, with the accusative of ﴿a people﴾. It was said: the substitute for the doer is the verbal noun of the verb, that is: "that recompense may be made to a people." It was said: the substitute is the prepositional phrase, as in the saying of the poet:

And if a poor woman bore a pup of a dog, the dogs would be cursed because of that pup.

Al-Akhfash and the Kufans permitted this, while the Basrans forbade it. The clause is a ground for the command to forgive. The people intended are the believers, who were commanded to forgive, so that Allah may recompense them on the Day of Resurrection for what they earned in the world of good deeds, among which is patience with the harm of the disbelievers, overlooking them, restraining anger, and enduring what is hateful.

It was said: the meaning is: that He may recompense the disbelievers for what they did of evil deeds, as if He said: "Do not repay them, so that We may repay them." The first is preferable.

Then He mentioned the believers and their deeds, and the polytheists and their deeds, saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for himself; and whoever does evil, it is against himself﴾. The meaning: the deed of each group, whether good or bad, does not go beyond its doer to another, and in this is encouragement and warning. ﴿Then to your Lord you will be returned﴾, so He will recompense each according to his deed: if it is good, then good, and if it is evil, then evil.

Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu al-Shaykh in "al-Azamah" reported through the route of Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿all of it from Him﴾, that he said: "From Him is the light, the sun, and the moon."

Ibn Jarir reported from him concerning the verse, that he said: "Everything is from Allah."

Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), and al-Bayhaqi in "al-Asma' wa al-Sifat" reported from Tawus, who said: A man came to Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As and asked him: "Of what was creation created?" He said: "Of water, light, darkness, air, and earth." He said: "Of what were these created?" He said: "I do not know."

Then the man came to ʿAbdullah ibn al-Zubayr and asked him, and he gave the same answer as ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr. Then he came to Ibn ʿAbbas and asked him, "From what were the creatures created?" He said, "From water, light, darkness, wind and earth." He said, "From what were these created?" Ibn ʿAbbas then recited: ﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, all of it from Him﴾. The man said, "None could have brought this except a man from the household of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Say to those who believe that they should forgive﴾ up to the end of the verse, that he said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to turn away from the polytheists when they harmed him, and they used to mock him and deny him. So Allah commanded him to fight the polytheists entirely, and this is among the abrogated (mansukh) rulings.

﴿And We certainly gave the Children of Israel the Book, the judgement (al-hukm) and prophethood, and We provided them with good things and preferred them over the worlds﴾. ﴿And We gave them clear proofs concerning the matter, and they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of rivalry among themselves. Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ﴾. ﴿Then We placed you on a path (shari'ah) of the matter, so follow it, and do not follow the desires of those who do not know﴾. ﴿Indeed they will not avail you anything against Allah. And indeed the wrongdoers are allies of one another, while Allah is the Ally of the God-fearing﴾. ﴿This is insight for mankind, and guidance and mercy for a people who have certainty﴾. ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will treat them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal in their living and their dying? Evil is their judgement﴾. ﴿And Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth, and so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged﴾. ﴿Have you seen him who takes his own desire as his god, and Allah has led him astray knowingly, and has sealed his hearing and his heart, and placed a covering over his sight? Who then will guide him after Allah? Will you not take heed?﴾ ﴿And they say: "There is nothing but our life of this world; we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time." And they have no knowledge of that; they only conjecture﴾. ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, their only argument is to say: "Bring our fathers, if you are truthful."﴾ ﴿Say: "Allah gives you life, then makes you die, then gathers you to the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt," but most people do not know﴾.

His saying: ﴿And We certainly gave the Children of Israel the Book, the judgement and prophethood﴾. The Book here is the Torah; the judgement (al-hukm) is the understanding and jurisprudence (fiqh) by which judgement is made among people and their disputes are settled; prophethood refers to those prophets whom Allah sent among them. ﴿And We provided them with good things﴾, i.e., the delightful things which Allah made lawful for them, among which were the manna and the quails. ﴿And preferred them over the worlds﴾, i.e., over the people of their time, since We gave them what We did not give to others besides them, such as the splitting of the sea and the like.

The explanation of this has already preceded in Surat al-Dukhan.

﴿And We gave them clear proofs concerning the matter﴾, i.e., clear laws concerning the lawful and the unlawful, or manifest miracles. It was also said: knowledge of the sending of the Prophet (ﷺ), the signs of his prophethood, and the specification of his place of migration. ﴿So they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them﴾, i.e., the disagreement among them about that matter occurred only after knowledge had come to them through its explanation and clarification of its meaning; thus they made what should have removed disagreement into the cause of its establishment. It was said: the "knowledge" here refers to Yusha ibn Nun, for some of them believed in him and some disbelieved. It was also said: it refers to the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), and they differed about it out of envy and rivalry. It was also said: rivalry among some of them against others, through seeking leadership. ﴿Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ﴾ regarding matters of religion, rewarding the doer of good for his good and the doer of evil for his evil.

﴿Then We placed you on a path (shari'ah) of the matter﴾. Shari'ah linguistically means a way (madhhab), a creed (millah) and a method (minhaj); it is said of the watering-place of water, which is the place where its drinkers come, a shari'ah; and from it comes "al-shari'" (the legislator), because it is a path to the goal. So the meaning of shari'ah here is what Allah prescribed for His servants of the religion, and its plural is shara'i'. That is: We placed you, O Muhammad, upon a clear method of the matter of religion that brings you to the truth, so follow it and act by its rulings with your community. ﴿And do not follow the desires of those who do not know﴾, i.e., the monotheism of Allah and His laws for His servants; they are the disbelievers of Quraysh and whoever agreed with them.

﴿Indeed they will not avail you anything against Allah﴾, i.e., they cannot repel from you anything of what Allah intends for you if you follow their desires. ﴿And indeed the wrongdoers are allies of one another﴾, i.e., helpers, each supporting the other. Ibn Zayd said: the hypocrites are allies of the Jews. ﴿While Allah is the Ally of the God-fearing﴾, i.e., their helper; and by "the God-fearing" are meant those who guarded against polytheism and sins.

The demonstrative in His saying "This" refers either to the Qur'an or to following the shari'ah. It is the subject, and its predicate is "is insight for mankind", i.e., proofs and indications for them concerning what they need of the rulings of religion; He made it as insight in the hearts. It is also read "these are insights", i.e., these verses, since the Qur'an has the same meaning as them, as the poet said:

"Ask the Banu Asad what this sound (al-sawt) is,"

since al-sawt means the cry. ﴿And guidance﴾, i.e., right direction and a path leading to Paradise for whoever acts by it. ﴿And mercy﴾ from Allah in the Hereafter, ﴿for a people who have certainty﴾, i.e., it is their nature to have certainty and to be free of doubt and wavering by doubts.

﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think﴾. "Am" here is the disjunctive one, presumed to be with "bal" and the hamzah; what is in it of the meaning of "bal" indicates the transition from the first statement to the second, and the hamzah is for denouncing the supposition. "Ijtirah" means acquiring, and from it comes "al-jawarih" (the limbs); it was mentioned in Surat al-Ma'idah. The sentence is resumed to explain the contrast between the two states of evildoers and doers of good, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿that We would treat them like those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, i.e., We would make them equal, despite their committing evil deeds, with the people of good deeds. ﴿Equal in their living and their dying﴾ in the abode of this world and in the Hereafter. "No, they are not equal, for the state of the people of felicity in both is other than the state of the people of wretchedness."

It was also said: the meaning is a denial that they would be equal in dying as they were equal in living.

The majority read "sawaʾun" with raising, as a predicate preceding its subject, the subject being "their living and their dying", and the meaning: a denial of their supposition that their living and their dying are equal. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read "sawaʾan" with the accusative, as a state of the pronoun hidden in the preposition-and-object in His saying "like those who believe", or as a second object of "hasiba". Abu ʿUbayd preferred the accusative reading and said its meaning is "We would make them equal." Al-Aʿmash and ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar read "mamatahum" with the accusative, meaning "equal in their living and their dying"; when the preposition was dropped, it took the accusative; or it is a substitute of the object of "najʿaluhum", a substitution of inclusion. ﴿Evil is their judgement﴾, i.e., evil is this judgement of theirs which they passed.

﴿And Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth﴾, i.e., with the truth that requires justice among the servants. The place of "bi-al-haqq" is accusative as a state of the agent or of the object, or the "ba'" is causal. His saying ﴿and so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned﴾ may be upon the truth, since each of them is a cause, so He joined a cause to a cause; it may also be conjoined to an omitted element, the estimate being: Allah created the heavens and the earth so that by them He might show His power, and so that they may be recompensed; and the lam may be of result. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾, i.e., the souls indicated by "every soul" will not be wronged by a reduction of reward or an increase of punishment.

Then He, glorified is He, marvelled at the state of the disbelievers, saying: ﴿Have you seen him who takes his desire as his god?﴾ Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: that disbeliever takes as his religion whatever he desires, so he does not desire anything without pursuing it. ʿIkrimah said: he worships what he desires or finds good; when he finds something good and it pleases him, he takes it as a god.
