Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: one of them would worship a stone, and when he saw something better than it he would discard it and worship the other. ﴿And Allah has led him astray knowingly﴾, i.e., with a knowledge He had. It was said: the meaning is: He led him astray from reward with knowledge on His part that he does not deserve it. Muqatil said: with knowledge from Him that he is astray, because He knows that the idol neither benefits nor harms.

Al-Zajjaj said: "with ill in His knowledge," that he is astray before He created him. The place of "ʿalā ʿilmin" is accusative as a state of the agent or the object. ﴿And He has sealed his hearing and his heart﴾, i.e., He stamped upon his hearing so that he does not hear the admonition, and stamped upon his heart so that he does not comprehend guidance. ﴿And placed a covering over his sight﴾, i.e., a veil, so that he does not see right direction.

The majority read "ghishawatan" with an alif and a kasra on the ghayn. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "ghashwatan" without alif and with a fatha on the ghayn, and from it is the poet's saying:

"If you had clothed me in a covering (ghashwah), I had certainly, for a while, inclined to you in affection."

Ibn Mas'ud and al-A'mash read like the majority's reading with a fatha on the ghayn, and this is the dialect of Rabi'ah. Al-Hasan and ʿIkrimah read it with a damma, and this is the dialect of ʿUkl. ﴿Then who will guide him after Allah?﴾, i.e., after Allah's misguiding him. ﴿Will you not take heed?﴾, a heeding of consideration, so that you may know the reality of the situation.

Then He, glorified is He, explained some of their ignorance and their errors, saying: ﴿And they say: "There is nothing but our life of this world"﴾, i.e., life is nothing but this life in which we are. ﴿We die and we live﴾, i.e., death befalls us and life in it; there is no life beyond that. It was said: we die ourselves, and our children live after us. It was said: we are first non-living drops, then we become living.

It was also said: there is inversion and reversal in the verse, i.e., "we live and we die", and Ibn Mas'ud read it so. In any case, their purpose in this saying is the denial of resurrection and the denial of the Hereafter. ﴿And nothing destroys us except time (al-dahr)﴾, i.e., nothing but the passing of days and nights. Mujahid said: he means years and days. Qatadah said: nothing but lifespan (al-ʿumr); the meaning is the same. Qutrub said: the meaning is "nothing destroys us except death". ʿIkrimah said: "nothing destroys us except Allah."

﴿And they have no knowledge of that﴾, i.e., they did not utter this saying except as doubters, not knowing the reality.

Then He explained that this proceeded from them and not from knowledge, saying: ﴿They only conjecture﴾, i.e., they are a people whose utmost is conjecture, so they speak only by it and rely only upon it.

﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them﴾, i.e., when the verses of the Qur'an are recited to the polytheists, being clear, manifest in meaning and in indication regarding resurrection, ﴿their only argument is to say: "Bring our fathers, if you are truthful" that we will be raised after death﴾, i.e., they had no argument nor any clinging except this false saying, which is not an argument in anything; he called it an argument only mockingly toward them.

The majority read "ḥujjatahum" with the accusative as the predicate of "kāna", with its subject being "illā an qālū". Zayd ibn ʿAli, ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmar read "ḥujjatuhum" with the nominative, as the subject of "kāna".

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to respond to them, saying: ﴿Say: "Allah gives you life"﴾, i.e., in this world, ﴿then makes you die﴾ at the end of your terms, ﴿then gathers you to the Day of Resurrection﴾ by the raising and the rising, ﴿about which there is no doubt﴾, i.e., concerning your gathering; for whoever is able to originate creation is able to restore it. ﴿But most people do not know﴾ this, and therefore doubt about resurrection arose in them, and they came up in repelling it with what is weaker than the spider's web. Had they looked with proper looking, they would have attained certain knowledge, the doubt would have left them, and they would have relieved themselves from the entanglement of doubt and bewilderment.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Then We placed you on a path of the matter﴾, that he said: "upon guidance in the matter of his religion."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿equal in their living and their dying﴾, that he said: "The believer is a believer in this world and the Hereafter, and the disbeliever is a disbeliever in this world and the Hereafter."

Al-Shawkani, *Fath al-Qadir*, on surah 45, verses 16–27 (part 3 of 3):

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Asma' wa al-Sifat* narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Have you seen him who has taken his desire as his god?﴾ He said: "That is the disbeliever who took his religion without guidance from Allah or any proof." ﴿And Allah has misled him with knowledge﴾ means: He misled him in His prior knowledge.

Al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, who declared it authentic (ṣaḥḥaḥahu), and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him that he said: "A man among the Arabs used to worship a stone. Whenever he found something better than it, he would take that and throw away the other. So Allah revealed: ﴿Have you seen him who has taken his desire as his god?﴾"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Hurayrah that he said: "The people of the Jahiliyyah used to say, 'Only the night and the day destroy us.' So Allah said in His Book: ﴿And they said, 'There is nothing but our life of this world: we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time.'﴾ Allah said: 'The son of Adam harms Me; he curses time, while I am time. In My hand is the affair; I turn the night and the day.'"

Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'The son of Adam harms Me; he curses time, while I am time. In My hand is the affair; I turn the night and the day.'"

**Fath al-Qadir of al-Shawkani, on verses 28–37 of Surah al-Jathiyah (45):**

When He (glory be to Him) mentioned what the polytheists argued with and how He answered them, He mentioned His exclusive dominion, saying: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth.﴾ That is, He alone disposes of them, and none of His servants shares in this.

Then He threatened the people of falsehood, saying: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, that Day the falsifiers will be lost.﴾ That is, the deniers, the disbelievers, those who cling to falsehoods. Their loss will become evident on that Day, because they will proceed to the Fire. The governing element (al-'amil) of "yawma" (on the day) is "yakhsaru" (will be lost), and "yawma'idhin" (on that day) is a substitute (badal) for it. The tanwin in "yawma'idhin" stands in place of the omitted genitive complement (al-mudaf ilayhi), which is indicated by what follows the substituted noun. So the implied sense is: "And on the Day the Hour is established, on the Day the Hour is established." This makes it a confirmatory substitute (badal tawkidi). The better view, however, is that the governing element of "yawm" is "mulk" (dominion), meaning: "And to Allah belongs the dominion on the Day the Hour is established," and "yawma'idhin" is the object (ma'mul) of "yakhsaru."

﴿And you will see every nation kneeling.﴾ The address is to everyone who is fit to receive it, or it is addressed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family). "Ummah" means religious community (millah). The meaning of "jathiyah" is "mustawfizah," that is, one who is poised with only his knees and the tips of his toes touching the ground. This is the posture at the reckoning.

It has also been said that the meaning of "jathiyah" is "gathered together." al-Farra' said: the meaning is "you will see the people of every religion gathered together." 'Ikrimah said: "separated from others." Mu'arrij said: in the language of Quraysh it means "humbled." al-Hasan said: "sitting upon their knees." Al-juthuw means sitting upon the knees; one says "jatha yajthu, yujthi, juthwan, and jithiyyan" when someone sits upon his knees. The first meaning is the better one.

This does not conflict with the use of this word in another sense in the language of the Arabs.

The word "juthwah" is used in Arabic for a group or heap of anything. Among its uses is the verse of Tarafah describing two graves:

*You see two heaps of earth over them, with solid slabs of arranged stone.*

The apparent meaning of the verse is that this description applies to every nation, without distinction between the people of the religions that followed the messengers and the polytheists.

Yahya ibn Salam said: it applies only to the disbelievers. The first view is the better one.

This is supported by His saying: ﴿Every nation will be called to its record.﴾ and by His saying later: ﴿As for those who believed...﴾ "To its record" means to the Book revealed to it. It has also been said: to the record of its deeds; it has also been said: to its reckoning; and it has also been said: the Preserved Tablet. The first view is the better one.

The majority of readers read "kullu ummatin" with a nominative (raf') as the subject (mubtada'), with its predicate being "tud'a" (will be called). Ya'qub al-Hadrami read it with an accusative (nasb) as a substitute (badal) for "kulla ummah": ﴿Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do.﴾ That is, it will be said to them: "Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do," of good and evil.

﴿This is Our Book, speaking against you with truth.﴾ This is part of what is said to them. The speakers are the angels. It has also been said that it is the word of Allah (glory be to Him), meaning that it bears witness against you. This is a metaphor (isti'arah). One says "the book spoke of such-and-such," meaning it made clear. It has also been said that they will read it and recall what they did, so it is as if it speaks against them with the truth, which has neither addition nor deficiency. The position of "yantiqu" is accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal), or nominative as another predicate of the demonstrative. The clause ﴿Indeed, We used to have copied what you used to do.﴾ gives the reason for "speaking with truth," meaning: We commanded the angels to copy (nash) your deeds, that is, to write them down and record them against you.

al-Wahidi said: most exegetes hold that this copying is from the Preserved Tablet, for the angels write from it each year what will occur of the deeds of the children of Adam, and they find it corresponding to what they do. They said: because copying can only be from an original.

It has also been said: the meaning is that We command the angels to copy what you used to do. It has also been said: the angels write down each day what the servant does; then when they return to their place they copy from it the good and bad deeds and leave aside the permissible ones.

It has also been said: when the angels raise the deeds of the servants to Allah (glory be to Him), He (mighty and majestic) commands that what contains reward and punishment be preserved with Him, and what contains neither reward nor punishment be dropped.

﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy.﴾ That is, admission into His mercy. ﴿That is the clear triumph.﴾ That is, the manifest and evident one.

﴿And as for those who disbelieved: "Were not My verses recited to you?"﴾ That is, it will be said to them this, and it is a rhetorical question of rebuke, because the messengers came to them and recited to them the signs of Allah, but they denied them and did not act upon them. ﴿But you were arrogant and were a criminal people.﴾ That is, you became proud, refusing to accept them and to believe in them, and you were among the people of crime, which means sins. "Ijtiram" means earning, and one says: "So-and-so is the jarimah (provider) of his family," if he is their earner. So the criminal (mujrim) is one who earns sins by committing acts of disobedience.

﴿And when it was said, "Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, and the Hour, there is no doubt about it,"﴾ That is, His promise of resurrection and reckoning, or of everything He promised concerning future matters, is certain to come to pass, and the Hour, that is, the Resurrection, there is no doubt about its occurrence.

The majority read "wa-as-sa'atu" (and the Hour) with nominative, as a subject (mubtada'), or as coordinated (ma'tuf) with the position of the subject of "inna." Hamzah read it with accusative, coordinated with the subject of "inna."

﴿You said, "We do not know what the Hour is."﴾ That is, what is it? ﴿We only assume an assumption.﴾ That is, we guess a guess and imagine an imagining.

al-Mubarrad said: its estimated form is: "We only assume an assumption." It has also been said: the estimated form is: "We only assume that you assume an assumption." It has also been said: "in nazunnu" is implicitly equivalent to "na'taqidu" (we believe), meaning: "we hold no belief except a guess, not knowledge." It has also been said: the word "zannan" has an estimated adjective: that is, "only a clear assumption." It has also been said: "zann" can mean both knowledge and doubt, so it is as if they said: "we have no belief except doubt." ﴿And we are not certain.﴾ That is, we had no certainty about it, and we had with us only mere assumption that the Hour is coming.

﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they did,﴾ That is, the evils of their deeds will become apparent to them in the form they actually have. ﴿and what they used to mock will surround them.﴾ That is, the recompense of their deeds will encompass them and descend upon them by their entry into the Fire.

﴿And it will be said, "Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours."﴾ That is, We will leave you in the Fire, just as you abandoned action for this Day. He attributed the "meeting" to the "Day" in a broadened sense, because He attributed to a thing what occurs within it. ﴿And your refuge is the Fire,﴾ That is, your dwelling and your place of settlement, to which you return. ﴿and you have no helpers﴾ who would help you and so prevent the punishment from you.

﴿That is because you took the signs of Allah in mockery,﴾ That is, that punishment is because you took the Qur'an as mockery and play. ﴿and the worldly life deceived you.﴾ That is, it deceived you with its adornments and its falsehoods, so you thought there was no abode other than it, and no resurrection or rising again. ﴿So today they will not be brought out from it,﴾ That is, from the Fire.

The majority read "yukhrajuna" with a dammah on the yā' and a fathah on the rā', in the passive voice, in the third person, to demean them. ﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends,﴾ That is, they will not be asked to satisfy Allah, nor will they be asked to return to obedience to Allah, because on that Day repentance will not be accepted, nor will an excuse benefit.

The tanwin in "yawma'idhin" stands in place of the omitted genitive complement (al-mudaf ilayhi), which is indicated by what follows the substituted noun. So the implied sense is: "And on the Day the Hour is established, on the Day the Hour is established." This makes it a confirmatory substitute (badal tawkidi). The better view, however, is that the governing element of "yawm" is "mulk" (dominion), meaning: "And to Allah belongs the dominion on the Day the Hour is established," and "yawma'idhin" is the object (ma'mul) of "yakhsaru."

This does not conflict with the use of this word in another sense in the language of the Arabs.

Their loss will become evident on that Day, because they will proceed to the Fire. The governing element (al-'amil) of "yawma" (on the day) is "yakhsaru" (will be lost), and "yawma'idhin" (on that day) is a substitute (badal) for it. The tanwin in "yawma'idhin" stands in place of the omitted genitive complement (al-mudaf ilayhi), which is indicated by what follows the substituted noun. So the implied sense is: "And on the Day the Hour is established, on the Day the Hour is established." This makes it a confirmatory substitute (badal tawkidi). The better view, however, is that the governing element of "yawm" is "mulk" (dominion), meaning: "And to Allah belongs the dominion on the Day the Hour is established," and "yawma'idhin" is the object (ma'mul) of "yakhsaru."

﴿And you will see every nation kneeling.﴾ The address is to everyone who is fit to receive it, or it is addressed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family). "Ummah" means religious community (millah). The meaning of "jathiyah" is "mustawfizah," that is, one who is poised with only his knees and the tips of his toes touching the ground. This is the posture at the reckoning.

It has also been said that the meaning of "jathiyah" is "gathered together." al-Farra' said: the meaning is "you will see the people of every religion gathered together." 'Ikrimah said: "separated from others." Mu'arrij said: in the language of Quraysh it means "humbled." al-Hasan said: "sitting upon their knees." Al-juthuw means sitting upon the knees; one says "jatha yajthu, yujthi, juthwan, and jithiyyan" when someone sits upon his knees. The first meaning is the better one.

This does not conflict with the use of this word in another sense in the language of the Arabs.

The word "juthwah" is used in Arabic for a group or heap of anything. Among its uses is the verse of Tarafah describing two graves:

*You see two heaps of earth over them, with solid slabs of arranged stone.*

The apparent meaning of the verse is that this description applies to every nation, without distinction between the people of the religions that followed the messengers and the polytheists.

Yahya ibn Salam said: it applies only to the disbelievers. The first view is the better one.

This is supported by His saying: ﴿Every nation will be called to its record.﴾ and by His saying later: ﴿As for those who believed...﴾ "To its record" means to the Book revealed to it. It has also been said: to the record of its deeds; it has also been said: to its reckoning; and it has also been said: the Preserved Tablet. The first view is the better one.

The majority of readers read "kullu ummatin" with a nominative (raf') as the subject (mubtada'), with its predicate being "tud'a" (will be called). Ya'qub al-Hadrami read it with an accusative (nasb) as a substitute (badal) for "kulla ummah": ﴿Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do.﴾ That is, it will be said to them: "Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do," of good and evil.

﴿This is Our Book, speaking against you with truth.﴾ This is part of what is said to them. The speakers are the angels. It has also been said that it is the word of Allah (glory be to Him), meaning that it bears witness against you. This is a metaphor (isti'arah). One says "the book spoke of such-and-such," meaning it made clear. It has also been said that they will read it and recall what they did, so it is as if it speaks against them with the truth, which has neither addition nor deficiency. The position of "yantiqu" is accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal), or nominative as another predicate of the demonstrative. The clause ﴿Indeed, We used to have copied what you used to do.﴾ gives the reason for "speaking with truth," meaning: We commanded the angels to copy (nash) your deeds, that is, to write them down and record them against you.

al-Wahidi said: most exegetes hold that this copying is from the Preserved Tablet, for the angels write from it each year what will occur of the deeds of the children of Adam, and they find it corresponding to what they do. They said: because copying can only be from an original.

It has also been said: the meaning is that We command the angels to copy what you used to do. It has also been said: the angels write down each day what the servant does; then when they return to their place they copy from it the good and bad deeds and leave aside the permissible ones.

It has also been said: when the angels raise the deeds of the servants to Allah (glory be to Him), He (mighty and majestic) commands that what contains reward and punishment be preserved with Him, and what contains neither reward nor punishment be dropped.

﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy.﴾ That is, admission into His mercy. ﴿That is the clear triumph.﴾ That is, the manifest and evident one.

﴿And as for those who disbelieved: "Were not My verses recited to you?"﴾ That is, it will be said to them this, and it is a rhetorical question of rebuke, because the messengers came to them and recited to them the signs of Allah, but they denied them and did not act upon them. ﴿But you were arrogant and were a criminal people.﴾ That is, you became proud, refusing to accept them and to believe in them, and you were among the people of crime, which means sins. "Ijtiram" means earning, and one says: "So-and-so is the jarimah (provider) of his family," if he is their earner. So the criminal (mujrim) is one who earns sins by committing acts of disobedience.

﴿And when it was said, "Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, and the Hour, there is no doubt about it,"﴾ That is, His promise of resurrection and reckoning, or of everything He promised concerning future matters, is certain to come to pass, and the Hour, that is, the Resurrection, there is no doubt about its occurrence.

The majority read "wa-as-sa'atu" (and the Hour) with nominative, as a subject (mubtada'), or as coordinated (ma'tuf) with the position of the subject of "inna." Hamzah read it with accusative, coordinated with the subject of "inna."

﴿You said, "We do not know what the Hour is."﴾ That is, what is it? ﴿We only assume an assumption.﴾ That is, we guess a guess and imagine an imagining.

al-Mubarrad said: its estimated form is: "We only assume an assumption." It has also been said: the estimated form is: "We only assume that you assume an assumption." It has also been said: "in nazunnu" is implicitly equivalent to "na'taqidu" (we believe), meaning: "we hold no belief except a guess, not knowledge." It has also been said: the word "zannan" has an estimated adjective: that is, "only a clear assumption." He attributed the "meeting" to the "Day" in a broadened sense, because He attributed to a thing what occurs within it. ﴿And your refuge is the Fire,﴾ That is, your dwelling and your place of settlement, to which you return. ﴿and you have no helpers﴾ who would help you and so prevent the punishment from you.

﴿That is because you took the signs of Allah in mockery,﴾ That is, that punishment is because you took the Qur'an as mockery and play. ﴿and the worldly life deceived you.﴾ That is, it deceived you with its adornments and its falsehoods, so you thought there was no abode other than it, and no resurrection or rising again. ﴿So today they will not be brought out from it,﴾ That is, from the Fire.

The majority read "yukhrajuna" with a dammah on the yā' and a fathah on the rā', in the passive voice, in the third person, to demean them. ﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends,﴾ That is, they will not be asked to satisfy Allah, nor will they be asked to return to obedience to Allah, because on that Day repentance will not be accepted, nor will an excuse benefit.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Umar something similar to what was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas.

The majority read "yukhrajuna" with a dammah on the yā' and a fathah on the rā', in the passive voice, in the third person, to demean them. ﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends,﴾ That is, they will not be asked to satisfy Allah, nor will they be asked to return to obedience to Allah, because on that Day repentance will not be accepted, nor will an excuse benefit.

﴿So to Allah belongs all praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.﴾ None deserves praise besides Him.

The majority read "Rabbi" in the three positions with a genitive (jarr), as an adjective of the noble name (the Name of Allah). Mujahid, Humayd, and Ibn Muhaysin read it with nominative in all three positions, by estimating a subject (mubtada'), meaning: "He is the Lord of the heavens," and so on.

﴿And to Him belongs the majesty in the heavens and the earth,﴾ That is, the grandeur, the greatness, and the sovereignty. He specified the heavens and the earth because this is most apparent in them. ﴿and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ That is, the Mighty in His dominion, so none can overpower Him; the Wise in all His actions, sayings, and all His decrees.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad in Zawa'id al-Zuhd, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th narrated from 'Abdullah ibn Babah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family) said: "It is as if I see you on a mound short of Jahannam, kneeling." Then Sufyan recited: "And you will see every nation kneeling."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Umar regarding His saying: ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling﴾ that he said: Every nation will be with its prophet, until the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family) comes upon a mound that rises above all creation. That is the Praised Station.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿This is Our Book, speaking against you with truth﴾ that he said: It is the Mother of the Book, in which are the deeds of the children of Adam. ﴿Indeed, We used to have copied what you used to do﴾ — he said: They are the angels who copy the deeds of the children of Adam.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, with a similar meaning but at greater length, that a man stood up and said: "O Ibn 'Abbas, we did not think that this is what the angels write every day and night." Ibn 'Abbas said: "You are not an Arab people." ﴿Indeed, We used to have copied what you used to do.﴾ Is anything copied except from a book?

Ibn Jarir also narrated something similar from him.

Ibn Jarir narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib who said: Allah has angels who descend each day with something on which they write the deeds of the children of Adam.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Umar something similar to what was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: The guardian angels copy from the Mother of the Book what the children of Adam do, so a person only does what the angel has copied from the Mother of the Book. al-Hakim narrated something similar from him and declared it sound.

al-Tabarani also narrated from him regarding the verse, that he said: Allah entrusted His angels to copy from that year, in (p-1361) Ramadan, on the Night of Power, what will happen on earth of events until the same time of the following year. They then present it to the guardian angels of Allah over the servants on the evening of every Thursday, and they find what the guardians have raised corresponds to what is in their book, with neither addition nor deficiency.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him also regarding His saying: ﴿Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours﴾ that he said: "We abandon you."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat narrated from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family) said: "Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'Greatness is My cloak, and majesty is My garment; whoever contends with Me over either of them, I will cast him into the Fire.'"
